**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, licence scope).**

What I found in Section 2 (Grant of Rights):
- **Revocability — compliant.** §2.1 hosting licence is expressly "perpetual and irrevocable"; §2.2 internal-use licence is "royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual". Nothing permits Commerce One to revoke at will.
- **Transferability — compliant.** Each grant is "nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1)", and §14.1 permits assignment without consent on a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all related assets (competitor carve-out only), with the agreement binding successors and permitted assigns. That satisfies the preferred successor-transfer position.
- **Sublicensing to hosted end customers — compliant.** §2.1(iii)–(iv) permit unlimited Customer sublicences; §1.17 "Corio Servers" covers servers operated "by or for" Corio.
- **Affiliates and contractors — gap.** The term "Affiliate" appears nowhere in the agreement, and the internal-use grant is limited to "Corio's internal business operations", so our group companies and contractors acting on our behalf have no licence rights and no path to be added.

Redline (validated, ok:true): a single new §2.11 inserted after §2.10 extending the Section 2 licences to Corio's Affiliates and to contractors acting on Corio's behalf, with Corio responsible for their compliance, plus an inline "Affiliate" definition — the minimal edit that reaches the preferred position without reopening the favourable perpetual/irrevocable and assignment language. Fallback (Affiliates on written notice) is flagged in the comment.
